To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of Gbp5 mRNA and Gbp2b protein in skin of resistant strains was higher than in skin of highly susceptible strains and that the expression of both Gbps was increased in organs of both highly susceptible and resistant strains after L. major infection.

the Gbp2b/1 and Gbp-5 genes are upregulated in all strains of mice infected with Leishmania major, but the expression is higher in the resistant strains than in the susceptible strains, and the protein is co-localized with parasites in the skin of resistant and susceptible mice, suggesting an active role of these genes in controlling the infection.

the expression of GBP2b/Gbp2 and GBP5 is increased even in organs, which are clinically asymptomatic and that the co-localization between GBP2b/GBP2 and Leishmania parasites is observed in the skin of resistant and susceptible mice, but not in the skin of highly susceptible BALB/c mice.

the expression of Gbps in the skin of resistant and susceptible strains of mice is different, and this difference might be one of the mechanisms responsible for the different outcome of the Leishmania infection in these mice strains.
the Gbps are involved in the control of L. major infection and that their role is strain dependent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gbp2b/ Gbp1 gene cluster is regulated at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels and that this regulation is influenced by the genetic background.
the Gbp genes are regulated in a complex manner by genetic background, and that this may contribute to differences in susceptibility to L. major infection.

Gbpb2 and Gbp5 are upregulated in all strains, but that Gbp5 is not sufficient to control infection in highly susceptible mice, whereas Gbp2 is sufficient in resistant strains and in addition to Gbp5 in intermediate strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Gbp genes is regulated at the transcriptional level in response to L. major infection and that this is influenced by the genetic background of the host.
the Gbp2b/ Gbp1 gene-cluster is a major player in the control of L. major infection and that its expression is regulated by both genetic and inflammatory factors.

the Gbp2b gene is a potential candidate for the development of novel therapeutics for the treatment of leishmaniasi
